verdict.rationale: PostHog Desktop's own docs say its coding agents (Pi, Claude Code, Codex) can use "Other MCP servers for services such as issue trackers, design tools, and internal APIs," alongside PostHog's own MCP server. That is a first-party MCP-client capability, but it rests on a single thin mention, and the client role may come from the third-party agents rather than PostHog itself. Most of the other MCP evidence covers PostHog acting as an MCP server, which belongs to a different story. Missing for 10: documented steps for adding or configuring third-party MCP servers, MCP-client support in the web PostHog AI analyst or Slack agent, details on supported transports and auth, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
